gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-bengal: Striking Stencilia gives headings a structural, cut-metal look, with generous gaps where its curves end; Noto Sans Bengali sits beneath in sans-serif form. Its capitals barely rise above the lowercase, so a long paragraph runs smooth.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-bhaiks: Tight, rope-like coils! Noto Sans Bhaiksuki fills the body with swollen lowercase, and its open apertures keep every letter readable. gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Noto Sans Brahmi reads in a contemporary, open-ended way, with a high mean line and curves that never quite close up. Stencilia adds structural bite on top.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-buhid: Spacious gaps at the curve terminals give Stencilia its cut, structural look. Noto Sans Buhid does the quieter job, a modern plain sans with a high x-height and generous room between curve ends and stems.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-carian: Noto Sans Carian reads clean and crisp, its terminals held apart like open scissor blades. Stencilia is the one to turn heads with its structural gaps at the curves, while the sans-serif body simply carries the text along.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-chakma: Stencilia opens with structural, striking curves and gaps. Noto Sans Chakma handles the steadier work as a sans-serif, its lowercase packed up toward the caps and its s and c mouths left uncrowded.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-cham: Stencilia brings a striking, structural look, with spacious gaps at its curve terminals. Noto Sans Cham plays the modern sans, offering tall rounded lowercase and c shapes with plenty of entry space.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-cherok: Those spacious gaps at the curve ends make Stencilia look cut rather than drawn. Noto Sans Cherokee supplies a tall band of letters with short stalks above, so the heading's structure has a friendly text to sit over.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-choras: Noto Sans Chorasmian has a large x-height and short ascenders, with curves that stop short instead of closing in. Over a long passage it moves along briskly, a plain sans with a contemporary feel.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-coptic: Noto Sans Coptic reads clean and dense, its middle zone dominating each line. Stencilia's structural, striking gaps at the curves are the standout, set against the sans-serif's open s and c mouths.
